title: Consumer commands are judged by the acting participant's `@mandate` profile; `ia position` stays ungated
summary: Breaking: @inventarch/cli now judges `ia read` and `ia next` (move Observation), `ia validate` and `ia preview` (Verification), `ia author` (Synthesis), and `ia capture`, its `ia compile` alias, `ia project` and a workspace `ia host <host> --apply`, which writes the same projection (Execution), by the acting participant's mandate profile (runtime governingMandates, defaultActor and profileRefusal) before they read or write anything; a capture or project plan is judged as the effect it plans, while a host plan, `ia host --remove` (which restores editing) and `ia host claude --user` are not judged. Where 2.0.0 ran these commands unconditionally, five cases now refuse them at exit 1: authored mandates that do not grant the mode's move, or, for preview and author only, exclude the word they write (IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-MOVE, -WORD); several authored participants and no authored `composition.steward`, an installed steward counting as none (IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-ACTOR); a default actor, such as an authored steward the mandates do not name, that no governing mandate binds (IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-ACTOR); an admitted governing mandate the runtime cannot read, such as one with a child under `authority.moves`, which admission accepts (IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID, located at the mandate); and, whatever the actor, path or word, any authored `@mandate` that failed admission, a stated `authority.moves []` among them, or a refused `@agent` or `@workspace` an admitted mandate or workspace depends on, which admission now refuses (IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID located at that record, described in the mandate-admission note). `ia preview` and `ia author` also judge the mandates whose authority.covers selects the target file. As in the edit guard, the selection and the path are both keyed with db pathKey before the G06c match, so on win32 and darwin, where pathKey folds case whatever the volume, a covers entry claims the file in any letter case, including a covered directory that does not exist yet and an entry cased differently from the directory on disk, and on a case-sensitive directory there it also claims a sibling spelled in another case; on other platforms case is significant. A workspace `ia init` creates grants all five moves to its one participant, so its commands run as before, and a workspace with no governing mandate restricts nothing. `ia position` and every command outside those modes are not gated, so the governance position a refusal names always runs (a refusal at a mandate admission refused names the admission report, `ia report --root <root>`, a machine route no mandate gates, instead); neither are the Door's read, next and position operations (the MCP tools), the install, update and remove projection refresh, `ia-distribution validate`, `ia inspect` and the records route, `ia init`, and `ia host`'s plan, `--remove` and `--user`. Each gated command accepts --actor <agent> (a canonical identity, `@agent <name>` or a bare name), which must be an authored participant of the repository's `@workspace`: an authored `@agent` a mandate scoped to it names, or its `composition.steward` when that is an authored `@agent`; an installed steward is no default actor. Naming an actor is a local declaration, not authentication, accepted whether or not the workspace leaves the choice open: it resolves an open choice, or under a steward acts as another of the workspace's actors, and then that participant's own mandates are judged, which may be looser or stricter than the default actor's; it never lifts a move or excluded word those mandates state. Every refusal names one command that runs for the same actor in the same state: the governance position of the mandate concerned (for a mandate admission refused, `ia report --root <root>`); under an open choice, or for a default actor no governing mandate binds, the same command with --actor naming the first participant whose mandates allow it (for an `ia author` form without a usable --digest, its `ia preview` form, which prints the digest); for an --actor that names no participant, the same command without it where the default actor may run it (for an `ia author` form without a usable --digest, again its `ia preview` form). Once a command's profile allows it, a refusal it raises later is held to the same rule: a next command of a gated mode the profile refuses becomes the governance position, and one it allows carries the named --actor. `ia project --apply` and a workspace `ia host --apply` write the rendering their gated plan session made, planned again against the files: a file changed since the plan still refuses, but a source or mandate change made while the confirmation question waits is not picked up, and `ia doctor` then reports the projection outdated. The machine routes, every `ia scope` form, MACHINE_PROTOCOL versions 1 and 2 and the runtime's own refusals are unchanged. Limits: actor selection is not host authentication; a mandate restricts only the gated CLI commands, not the ungated surfaces above; the next-command rule holds for gated commands only, so an ungated command's refusal may name a gated command that then refuses with its own mandate refusal; the edit guard re-keyed to `@mandate`, which reads the same resolver, is described in its own note (generation-hook-governance).
